question: How often should a client receive a DMPA (Depo-Provera) injection for birth control?
explanation: You've got this! DMPA gives steady hormonal protection when given once every 3 months (about 13 weeks). [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h1)

question: How often must the injectable contraceptive NET-EN be given to keep working?
explanation: NET-EN uses a different progestin type that needs to be repeated every 2 months, which is 8 weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h1)

question: How does the progestin in injectable contraceptives mainly stop sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus to create a barrier
options.B: By neutralizing the natural acid inside the vagina
options.C: By dissolving sperm cells on contact
options.D: By causing the fallopian tubes to tie themselves

explanation: Think of it like a security guard: the hormone makes the cervical mucus thick and sticky so sperm can't swim up into the womb! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h2)

question: What is the main way injectable contraceptives prevent pregnancy in the body?

options.A: Increasing the movement of cilia in the fallopian tubes
options.B: Stimulating the immediate shedding of the uterine lining
options.C: Lowering total estrogen production in the adrenal glands
options.D: Stopping the release of an egg from the ovary

explanation: Spot on! Injectables mainly stop ovulation so there's no egg around to be fertilized in the first place. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h2)

question: Under the WHO medical rules, what does a Category 4 classification mean for a contraceptive method?

options.A: The benefits outweigh the risks in most cases
options.B: There are no restrictions on using the method
options.C: The method can be used with routine monitoring
options.D: The method represents an unacceptable health risk

explanation: Category 4 means 'Stop!' — the condition is too dangerous, and the contraceptive must not be used because it puts the client's health at serious risk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h3)

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?
explanation: Because breast cancer is sensitive to hormones, using hormonal contraceptives is unsafe and falls into the restricted Category 4. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h3)

question: Why should you advise a client NOT to massage her arm or buttock after a DMPA injection?

options.A: It pushes the liquid medicine directly into a blood vessel
options.B: It speeds up drug absorption and shortens protection
options.C: It stops the needle puncture wound from closing properly
options.D: It causes severe bruising on the skin surface

explanation: Massaging increases blood flow, making the body absorb the hormone too fast. That means it might wear off sooner than expected! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h4)

question: Which muscle is a safe, standard site for giving an intramuscular DMPA injection?
explanation: The ventrogluteal site is a fantastic choice because it has a thick muscle mass safely away from major nerves and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h4)

question: Why do some clients stop seeing their period (amenorrhea) while using progestin-only injections?

options.A: Thickening of the blood inside the uterus
options.C: Complete blockage of the cervical canal
options.D: Thinning and resting of the uterine lining

explanation: No regular estrogen means the uterine lining stays thin and relaxed, so there's barely any tissue to shed during a monthly period. Totally normal! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h5)

question: Which of these statements about injectable contraceptives is FALSE?

options.A: They prevent pregnancy by stopping ovulation
options.B: They require regular repeat doses to remain effective
options.C: They lead to permanent sterility after one dose
options.D: They can cause changes in monthly bleeding patterns

explanation: Injectables do not cause permanent infertility! Once you stop, fertility naturally returns after the drug clears the system. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h5)

question: A client panics in the clinic because she hasn't seen her period for 2 months after her first DMPA shot. What should you do?

options.A: Stop the injection immediately and switch her to pills
options.B: Tell her to take a pregnancy test every single week
options.C: Order an emergency surgical dilation and curettage procedure
options.D: Reassure her that absent periods are a common, harmless side effect

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Reassuring her that amenorrhea is a harmless side effect eases her mind and keeps her from dropping a great contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h6)

question: Why is it helpful to give a client a written appointment card after her injection?

options.A: To help ensure she returns on the correct date for her next dose
options.B: To prove to her family that she visited the clinic
options.C: To act as an emergency contraceptive pill if she misses a dose
options.D: To serve as a legal receipt for hospital service fees

explanation: A simple appointment card is a friendly reminder that helps clients stay on track and avoid missing their injection window. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h6)

question: What is normal regarding a woman's fertility after she stops taking DMPA injections?

options.A: Fertility returns instantly within twenty-four hours
options.B: There can be a delay of several months before ovulation resumes
options.C: Fertility is permanently destroyed after one year of use
options.D: Fertility only returns if surgical intervention is performed

explanation: Because the hormone lingers in the body tissues, it can take a few months for ovulation and regular cycles to bounce back after stopping. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h7)

question: What happens to a client's bone mineral density after she stops using injectable contraceptives?

options.A: It continues to drop rapidly until old age
options.B: It turns into permanent brittle bone disease instantly
options.C: It recovers fully over time after discontinuation

explanation: Bone density might dip a bit during use due to lower estrogen, but studies show the bone mass builds right back up once injections are stopped! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T013#GNS226_U6_T013_h7)
